axis.not_the_target: in-cell expression. The source table reports Ribosome load as a separate measured quantity and Predicted expression as a derived prediction. Neither is the target here.
axis.target: in-cell mRNA half-life (In-cell half-life / In-cell degradation coefficient), i.e. mRNA DECAY inside cells
axis.why_it_matters: The frozen STRAND calibration was fitted entirely on IN-SOLUTION labels, and the two axes rank at Spearman +0.0545 on identical constructs. The project's stability objective has therefore never been fitted to the axis the user wants.

bar.statement: A candidate is only interesting if it clears the free single feature on the held-out constructs.

measured_ribosome_load_ceiling.is_not_a_usable_feature: Ribosome load is a MEASUREMENT and cannot be an input in production. It is carried to bound what wiring RiboNN's predicted translation efficiency into the stability model could buy. RiboNN's prediction is necessarily weaker than the measurement, so this is an upper bound, not an expectation.
measured_ribosome_load_ceiling.verdict: the ceiling does not clear the transcript GC bar, so wiring RiboNN into the stability model is not worth building

multiplicity_warning: 37 features were screened on 105 training records. 14 cleared the bar on training and were scored once on the held-out set. With this many candidates and this few records, a training correlation above the bar is expected by chance for several features, which is why the held-out column is the only one that counts.
purpose: Find which features, if added to the RNAfold + STRAND + RiboNN + BoTorch combination, would improve prediction of IN-CELL mRNA stability. Transcript GC alone already reaches +0.2253 on the held-out constructs, so the bar is set by a free single feature.
screen_is_univariate_because: gate v15 measured that this label-set size supports about one feature: held-out correlation fell from +0.3651 at one feature to +0.1317 at four while training correlation rose to +0.5972

source.not_redistributed: Only the URL and both hashes are pinned, as for the RiboNN weights, the Rfam sources and the mRNAutilus checkpoint. The archive and table are not copied into this repository.

split.note: The preserved split keeps the two-axis comparison's 122-record held-out set, so no in-cell label that this project has already used is reused. It cannot screen UTR features: its training half is 78 of 81 CDS (Nluc) variants, which hold the UTRs fixed, so utr5_gc takes 2 distinct values in training against 46 in the held-out set, and every UTR feature is near-constant. This run therefore REDRAWS the split, balanced within each design family at seed 1729. The amendment is recorded rather than applied silently. It departs from the protocol's declared 'preserve the existing split' clause, for the reason above. Consequence to carry: an in-cell result on this split is NOT comparable to the in-solution results, which keep the 122-record set, and any future in-cell claim must state which split it used.

what_this_cannot_establish: No resolution claim. Every predictor tested in this project so far sits at chance below 1.10x, and a univariate screen will not change that.
Nothing about in-cell expression, which is not the target here and is not measured by the in-cell half-life columns.
No claim that a promoted feature improves the production path. The screen does not fit, adopt or wire anything.
Nothing about whether the in-cell orthogonality or these feature rankings hold for endogenous mRNAs rather than designed reporter constructs.
